incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 347, as amended; Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, as amended (default general partnership rules) applicable sections concerning creation, filing, registration and amendment of a limited partnership declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Corporate Online; Service BC; Ministry of Finance
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Declaration (Form 1) filed under the British Columbia Limited Partnership Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Limited Partnership Act. Capital contributions are fixed contractually in the Limited Partnership Agreement. No escrow account is mandated unless limited partnership interests are distributed under a BC Securities Act prospectus exemption requiring segregation of subscription proceeds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the General Partner approves the initial subscription of limited partnership interests by the Founding Limited Partner, comprising cash and services as set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement; (2) the registered office and records address of the Limited Partnership be established at [Registered Office Address], British Columbia, and the first keeper of corporate records be appointed; (3) [Name] be and is hereby appointed General Partner with authority to bind the Limited Partnership, and [Name] be appointed Chief Operations Officer, with authority to open bank accounts, execute employment and payroll documents, and file all regulatory licences; (4) all partners and officers are directed to execute all ancillary instruments for compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for the proposed limited partnership name and submit a Name Reservation Request through BC Registries Corporate Online. Use the returned Name Reservation Number as a preliminary condition for filing the Limited Partnership Declaration.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name and business description
Consent of the proposed General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or queried, file an amended name reservation or adopt a numbered limited partnership style and refile the request within the Registry notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and commissioning notary public (internal drafting and execution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement, capital account schedule, interests and allocations, management provisions, and authority of the General Partner. Notarize or commission all wet-ink signatures where electronic execution is not accepted.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent from address provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance term is questioned by any partner, amend by written unanimous consent and attach a certificate of amendment before filing the Declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Limited Partnership Declaration and Initial Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies via BC Registries Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Limited Partnership Declaration with the approved name or numbered designation, registered office address, full legal names and addresses of all general partners and limited partners, and statement of liability limitation. Pay the statutory filing fee and obtain the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the Declaration, provide amended particulars by filing a correction or amendment declaration within the statutory cure period and pay the applicable amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal CRA Business Number, GST/HST and Payroll Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a Business Number through CRA Business Registration Online, requesting RT (GST/HST), RP (Payroll), and RC (Corporation tax information return where applicable). Link the BC Limited Partnership as the taxpayer entity.
required_dossiers: Legal name and address of the General Partner
Canada Revenue Agency identification of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA issues a query or inconsistency, call the Business Registration Helpdesk, provide the assigned Business Number, and file Form RC1 with supporting partnership records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Employer Registration and WorkSafeBC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Ministry of Finance and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the BC Ministry of Finance for provincial employer and income tax accounts, and register as an employer with WorkSafeBC for workers' compensation obligations. Assign the correct industry classification for staffing and EOR services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an industry classification or clearance dispute arises, submit an employer self-assessment and request review or reclassification by WorkSafeBC within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employment Agency and Temporary Help Agency Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Employment Standards Branch, Ministry of Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Temporary Help Agency Licence under the British Columbia Employment Standards Act and related Temporary Help Agency Licensing Regulation. Provide corporate particulars, evidence of Workers' Compensation coverage and compliance undertaking, and pay the licence fee.
required_dossiers: Business plan and staffing service description
Security, bond, or irrevocable letter of credit if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence application is queried, supply corrective explanations, amend the schedule of services, and respond with supporting affidavits within the Branch's stated deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Physical Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government business licence office and building inspection department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal business licence application for the registered office and operations premises, submit a certified floor plan, obtain occupancy / fire inspection sign-off, and confirm lawful use of the leased premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality withholds approval, correct any building code non-conformities, obtain revised structural or fire inspection reports, and re-apply as an office use only.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Clearance and Records Management Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy and municipal environmental health officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm exemption from a full Environmental Assessment Certificate for a low-risk service office, register any confidential records destruction stream with the applicable municipal environmental health office, and establish waste handling manifests.
required_dossiers: Records destruction and recycling vendor contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental health officer requires a remediation or compliance plan, submit a short-term corrective plan and re-inspection request within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: BC Employment Standards Branch; WorkSafeBC; local municipal business licence office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Temporary Help Agency Licence under the British Columbia Employment Standards Act and Temporary Help Agency Licensing Regulation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category C low-risk service office: no full Environmental Assessment Certificate required for an employer-of-record and payroll office; municipal environmental health approval and Recycling Regulation registration may apply for records destruction streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or volatile organic compound emissions; sanitary sewage to municipal sewer; stormwater discharge must meet municipal by-law limits; confidential paper and electronic media must be recycled through registered vendors in compliance with the BC Recycling Regulation; no on-site fuel storage or hazardous waste generation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance under the BC Building Code and Fire Code, including smoke detection, fire extinguisher, and emergency exit certification; structural load inspection for the leased office floor as certified by the landlord or a structural engineer; mandatory WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and first aid equipment compliance under Part 3 of the Workers Compensation Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal consumption and income tax administration: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, Business Registration Online portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/business.html. Provincial consumption tax administration: British Columbia Ministry of Finance, e-Tax BC portal at https://etax.gov.bc.ca. Entity registration: BC Corporate Registry at https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca. GST/HST and federal payroll accounts are administered by CRA; PST is administered exclusively by British Columbia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the limited partnership under the British Columbia Limited Partnership Act, or extra-provincially if the LP is formed in another province, through the BC Corporate Registry. Step 2: Obtain the partnership's 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online by selecting the 'Partnership' entity type and supplying the general partner's SIN or BN; a non-resident general partner must provide a Canadian address for service. Step 3: Activate required federal program accounts under the same BN: RT (GST/HST) once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters, and RP (payroll source deductions) because the LP is the employer of record for Canadian employees. Step 4: Register separately for BC PST through e-Tax BC before making taxable retail sales or leases in BC; PST has no small-supplier threshold applicable to EOR service fees. Step 5: File the annual T5013 Statement of Partnership Income within five months of the partnership's fiscal year end, file the BC LP annual report, and ensure each partner reports their allocated share of Canadian-source and worldwide income on their own returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - Under section 96 of the Income Tax Act (Canada), a BC Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent: the partnership computes income and loss at the partnership level but is not a taxpayer, and each partner is taxable on their allocated share. For GST/HST and BC PST, however, the LP is a separate 'person' and a distinct registrant in its own right. Territorial scope: partners resident in Canada are taxable on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxable only on Canadian-source income, including income attributable to a permanent establishment in Canada, subject to applicable tax treaty relief. Income earned through a foreign permanent establishment is allocated to partners and taxed according to each partner's residency status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada operates no check-the-box or elective entity-classification regime; the transparent status of an LP is statutory. Available elections and mechanisms applicable to the BC LP include: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration by a small supplier with taxable supplies of CAD 30,000 or less (Excise Tax Act section 241(1)); (ii) election of the GST/HST Quick Method of accounting, with CRA approval, for eligible small businesses; (iii) election of a non-calendar GST/HST filing period and annual filing where CRA consent is obtained; and (iv) for non-resident partners, reliance on tax treaty residence and permanent-establishment determinations. Hybrid and mismatch arrangements involving allocations to non-resident partners are constrained not by election but by the general anti-avoidance rule (section 245 of the Income Tax Act), the foreign accrual property income (FAPI) rules, and transfer-pricing rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a federal value-added tax at 5%, combined with British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST), a single-stage retail sales and use tax at 7%; British Columbia does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) system. In a global EOR arrangement, the service fee constitutes consideration for a taxable supply unless zero-rated as an export; wage and payroll disbursement payments made under the employer-of-record relationship are not supplies and attract neither GST nor PST. British Columbia also imposes the Employer Health Tax (2.925% of total BC remuneration exceeding CAD 1,500,000) as a separate payroll levy, not an indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies over any four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold). EOR service fees count as consideration for this test, and GST registration is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded. PST: nil threshold; registration with the BC Ministry of Finance is mandatory before making taxable sales, leases, or provisions of services in British Columbia, including sale-through-agent and marketplace arrangements involving foreign principals.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API e-invoice clearance regime. CRA requires GST-registered suppliers to issue invoices meeting the substantive requirements of sections 221 to 223 of the Excise Tax Act: for taxable supplies exceeding CAD 30, the invoice must state the supplier's name and GST/HST registration number, the recipient's name, the consideration, the tax charged or a zero-rating statement, and the date of issue. Electronic invoicing in EDI, XML, PDF, or structured formats aligned with the pan-Canadian e-invoicing standard (E-Inv) is accepted voluntarily; no pre-clearance approval is required. BC PST rules generally require the seller's PST number on invoices and separate disclosure of PST where the vendor is registered; no government stamping applies. CRA audit tools include electronic sales suppression detection and full data extraction from payroll systems and payment rails such as direct deposit and Wise.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exported tangible personal property is zero-rated under section 1 of Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the property is exported by or on behalf of the LP and the LP maintains prescribed evidence of export. Services: a supply of a service to a non-resident person is zero-rated under section 7 of Part V of Schedule VI, unless an exclusion applies. The principal exclusions are: (a) the non-resident recipient is registered for GST/HST under Subdivision d of Division V of Part IX; (b) the service relates to real property situated in Canada; (c) the service is supplied in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; (d) the service is rendered to an individual present in Canada; or (e) litigation-related services. For a global EOR platform providing cross-border employer-of-record administration and contractor payroll services to a foreign client, the service fee is ordinarily zero-rated provided the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and the service does not relate to Canadian-situated real or tangible property; the service agreement must clearly separate the administrative fee from payroll disbursements and statutory withholdings.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Canadian export declaration (G7 or CAED electronic export reporting summary) with CBSA B13 or cargo-control confirmation for physical goods
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or waybill evidence naming the LP as exporter or shipper and identifying the foreign port of exit
Commercial invoices for exported goods or zero-rated services showing consideration, currency, incoterms, and the zero-rating indicator
Executed global EOR service agreement and itemized fee schedule separating the service fee from gross payroll, employer health tax, and payroll source deductions

Primary evidence of FX repatriation: SWIFT or Wise transaction receipts, foreign bank statements, or inward remittance certificates demonstrating receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident client; Canada imposes no statutory repatriation deadline, but 180 days is the documentary best-practice control period consistent with bank compliance and CRA audit expectations
Canadian payroll compliance records, including T4 statements of remuneration, PD7A source-deduction remittances, and Employer Health Tax returns, proving the LP's employer-of-record role
BC PST export-exemption certificates or PST return schedules supporting refunds of PST charged on goods removed from British Columbia
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating where the evidentiary bundle is incomplete, reassessing the supply at 5% GST within the normal four-year limitation period, which is extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud. Erroneous input tax credits recovered in connection with zero-rated exports are subject to repayment demands with statutory arrears interest. Gross-negligence and false-statement penalties under the Excise Tax Act generally equal 50% of the net tax understated or refund overclaimed, subject to statutory minimums. Willful evasion attracts criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. The BC Ministry of Finance may similarly claw back uncollected PST plus interest and impose a penalty of 25% of the tax for knowingly making a false statement. CRA and BC Finance coordinate audits of cross-border payroll and EOR arrangements, with particular scrutiny of back-to-back invoicing designed to convert taxable Canadian payroll administration into purported zero-rated export services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central monetary authority); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the financial intelligence and AML/CTF supervisory authority under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the prudential supervisor of federally regulated banks. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange control administration or central-bank licensing regime for FX transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada has no exchange-control legislation restricting the purchase, sale, or transfer of foreign currencies. Current-account payments, including payroll, contractor fees, and service disbursements, are free of any central-bank approval. Capital-account transactions, including contributions to a British Columbia limited partnership and profit/equity repatriation, are likewise unrestricted, subject to the Investment Canada Act review threshold for non-Canadian acquisitions of control of a Canadian business and Part XIII withholding tax on certain outbound payments. Partnership distributions to non-resident partners are remittable without prior consent; a 25% Part XIII withholding tax applies except where reduced by an applicable income tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable in Canada. There is no statutory obligation requiring exporters or service providers to surrender foreign-currency receipts to the Bank of Canada or to convert export proceeds into CAD within any specified timeline. Exporters and cross-border payees may hold foreign-currency bank accounts and repatriate funds freely, subject to general Canadian income tax reporting obligations and FINTRAC record-keeping for foreign exchange transactions above CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall feasibility rating: Medium. Canadian-regulated payment service providers and fintech platforms (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer) may support low-value cross-border contractor payroll disbursements; however, they are not licensed deposit-taking banks and cannot lawfully hold capital-escrow accounts or operational partnership funds as a substitute for a Schedule I chartered bank. Offshore digital EMI platforms that are not registered in Canada under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act are not viable standalone clearing rails for CAD-denominated payroll or statutory capital contributions. A compliant structure pairs a Canadian bank master account with a registered Money Service Business (MSB) licence and direct sub-ledger integration to trusted fintech clearing providers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for British Columbia limited partnerships. Most Schedule I Canadian banks accept a fully digital KYC package comprising video identification for all general partners and authorized signatories, electronic signatures on partnership agreements, and notarized corporate registry extracts. A physical bank branch visit is not a statutory requirement under federal banking rules, but banks retain discretion to require an in-person interview where the customer profile shows elevated ML/TF risk, high-volume non-resident funding, or sanctioned-jurisdiction connections. For a Global EOR staffing entity, a structured video KYC interview together with a completed Pre-Documentation Profile and business plan generally satisfies the bank's financial crime due diligence. Directors of non-resident corporate general partners may also be onboarded remotely subject to enhanced documentary verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners participating in a Canadian-registered partnership with no clearly evidenced economic nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified BC Limited Partnership registration statement, full beneficial-ownership schedule, GP agreement and LP subscription agreements, partnership tax allocation and distribution waterfall, source-of-wealth statements for each non-resident limited partner, bank reference letters, and authenticated corporate registry excerpts from the ultimate parent's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital transfers from foreign parent or affiliated EOR platform into a newly opened Canadian bank account, initially classified as 'unexpected' by the bank's transaction-monitoring system.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notice, board resolution authorizing the capital contribution, executed equity-contribution agreement, bank-to-bank reference, wiring instruction with explicit remittance narrative, inward-correspondent MT103 trace, completed FINTRAC large-money-transfer declaration if applicable, and an audited opening balance-sheet projection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll disbursements to beneficiaries in countries subject to sanctions, FATF targeted monitoring, or with high corruption indexes, creating a potential OFAC/Global Affairs Canada sanctions screening hit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions compliance policy and procedural manual, automated real-time OFAC/UN/Global Affairs Canada list screening screenshots, per-beneficiary contractor agreement and identity validation, rationale for legitimate EOR employment in the affected jurisdiction, transaction observation reports, and legal counsel sanction-blocking opinion confirming permissible lawful disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The EOR platform's high aggregate monthly payroll and payroll float balances being mischaracterized as money laundering or unlicensed remittance activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid BC Employment Agency licence under the Employment Standards Act, payroll trust account arrangement and audited trust account ledger, worker classification diagnostic (employee versus independent contractor), source payroll reports from the platform, Canadian payee T4/T4A-NR tax filings, FINTRAC MSB registration certificate where money remittance is performed, and an external AML compliance review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent or foreign limited partner to the BC LP is through a SWIFT MT103 originated by a foreign bank and received by the LP's Schedule I Canadian bank account. The wire should use a clearly descriptive purpose code and remittance narrative, e.g., 'Capital Contribution to Limited Partnership Account 1-234-ERP-001', together with the LP's registered name and business number. The bank will require evidence of the capital call, underlying partnership agreement, and beneficial ownership disclosure. Canadian banks apply PCMLTFA verification and may request the foreign financial institution to add a 'FOR FURTHER CREDIT TO' line on the MT103, ensuring traceability from the source account. High-value currencies should be settled over the relevant domestic high-value payment system and then routed onward, or directly via Canada's Lynx high-value payment system where the foreign bank has a Canadian correspondent relationship. No foreign-exchange approval is required, but the bank reserves the right to ensure the transaction's economic substance and to file a large transaction report / suspicious transaction report if warranted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and payroll disbursements may be executed via: (i) SWIFT MT103 wires for high-value cross-border contractor payments, professional fees, and settlement of invoices; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700 / UCP600) for merchandise or service trade settlements where shipment or performance security is required; (iii) Payments Canada ACSS direct deposit and payroll ACH rails for domestic CAD payroll runs; and (iv) real-time payment schemes offered by the bank or licensed fintech partners for low-value beneficiary payments. Cross-border wire forms must specify the final beneficiary's legal name, account number, SWIFT/BIC, and a full remittance-information field containing the invoice or pay-period reference. Anti-money-laundering measures require that the outbound originator information complies with FATF Recommendation 16 (travel rule), including full wire-transparency fields. For jurisdictions with restrictive FX controls, the EOR shall use CAD or USD settlement subject to sanctions screening and, where applicable, a non-deliverable forward hedge to manage exposure.

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards with a Schedule I Canadian bank or OSFI-supervised broker
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in CAD against emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX options (call and put spreads) traded on a recognized exchange or OTC with a licensed derivatives dealer
Currency futures listed on Bourse de Montréal Inc. (TMX Group) or a permitted foreign exchange, subject to commodity futures regulatory approvals

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Report (BC Registry Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / BC Registry Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary of registration of the limited partnership in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD$100; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off by the BC Registrar; restoration fees and a reactivation resolution may subsequently be required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013) and T5013/RL slips issued to all partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the calendar year-end; for a fiscal period ending other than December 31, on or before the 5th day of the 3rd month after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD$25 per partner per day (minimum CAD$100), capped at CAD$2,500; additional penalties may apply for gross negligence or if filed knowingly late.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for a British Columbia limited partnership under the Partnership Act. An independent audit may become mandatory if the partnership agreement or a lender/surety requires it, or if the BC Business Practices and Consumer Protection Authority (BPCPA) imposes audited financial statements as a condition of the employment agency/licensed temporary staffing service registration.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). ASPE is typically used for a private BC LP; IFRS is mandatory if the partnership is a Canadian reporting issuer or elected IFRS under NI 52-107.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing for limited partnerships. The LP must maintain a current and accurate register of limited partners at its registered office and record every transfer or withdrawal of a limited partner's interest immediately. The T5013 annual information return serves as the primary annual disclosure to CRA of partners' identities, addresses, and allocated amounts. Annually, the general partner should review the partner register, enter any changes, and file with the BC Registrar an amendment when the general partner changes or when the partnership agreement has been amended.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, capital contributions, transfer dates)
Minute book containing executed partnership resolutions and consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD$600–$1,200 (approx. USD$450–$900) for BC registered office plus annual filing agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD$6,000–$15,000 (approx. USD$4,500–$11,200) for a typical BC limited partnership employment agency with EOR payroll operations
